---

**1. INTRODUCTION**

1.1 This manual provides standard procedures, specifications, and safety information for the operation and maintenance of Press Line 3. It is intended for use by trained maintenance technicians, press operators, and shift supervisors.

1.2 All maintenance activities SHALL be carried out in accordance with the procedures in this manual. Any deviation from these procedures requires prior written authorisation from the Maintenance Manager.

1.3 The manual is divided into numbered sections. Section numbers are referenced throughout. Where a section has been revised, the revision stamp and date are shown in the footer of each page.

1.4 Any defects, missing parts, or suspected safety issues SHALL be reported immediately using the Exception Log (Form MP-EL-01) and the relevant section of this manual flagged for review.

---

**2. GENERAL SAFETY**

2.1 **Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) Procedure**

2.1.1 Before any maintenance, cleaning, or repair work is carried out, the following lockout procedure SHALL be followed:

a) Isolate the main electrical supply using the isolator switch located at the rear of the press, adjacent to the control cabinet. The switch is labelled "PL3 MAIN ISOLATOR". (Note: As of revision 1.4, this switch is a new red rotary type; the old toggle switch has been removed.)
b) Lock the isolator in the OFF position using a personal padlock. Each technician SHALL use their own lock and key.
c) Depress and lock the pneumatic isolation valve on the air supply line (red valve, located near the floor on the left-hand side of the press).
d) If work is to be carried out on the blanket cylinders or the impression cylinder, also isolate the hydraulic supply and lock the pressure release valve.
e) Verify that all moving parts have come to a complete stop before proceeding.
f) Place a "DANGER - DO NOT OPERATE" tag on the main isolator and on the control panel.

2.1.2 Only the person who fitted a lock may remove it. If a lock is left on and the person has gone off shift, the shift supervisor SHALL verify the situation and may remove the lock only after ensuring it is safe to do so, and the removal SHALL be logged in the Exception Log.

The Maintenance Manual - Press Line 3 states that the scheduled_overhaul_date for Press Line 3 is 2023-08-14. Record status: superseded.

2.1.3 On completion of work, remove all tools and materials, check that no personnel are in the danger zone, and then remove locks and tags in the reverse order of fitting.

2.2 **Emergency Stop**

2.2.1 There are three red emergency stop buttons on Press Line 3: one at the feeder end, one at the delivery end, and one on the main control panel. Pressing any one of these SHALL immediately cut power to all drives and stop the press.

2.2.2 After an emergency stop, the cause SHALL be investigated before restarting. The restart procedure is described in Section 3.4.

---

**3. OPERATING PROCEDURES**

3.1 **Start-Up Sequence (Normal)**

a) Ensure all guards are in place and secure.
b) Check that the LOTO tags are clear (if any work has been carried out).
c) Turn on the main isolator.
d) Turn on the air supply at the main valve.
e) Switch on the control panel power.
f) Wait for the touchscreen to initialise (approx. 30 seconds).
g) Perform the "Pre-Start Checklist" displayed on the touchscreen. This includes checking ink levels, blanket pressure, and web alignment.
h) Press "START" on the touchscreen. The press will slowly rotate and then speed up to the set speed.

3.2 **Shut-Down Sequence**

a) Stop the web feed using the "WEB STOP" button.
b) Run the press at low speed for 2 minutes to clear the last of the web.
c) Apply the blanket wash cycle (see Section 6.2).
d) Press "STOP" on the touchscreen.
e) Switch off the control panel power.
f) Turn off the air supply.
g) Turn off the main isolator.

3.3 **Emergency Restart After E-Stop**

3.3.1 If an emergency stop has been activated, the following steps SHALL be taken:

a) Investigate and rectify the cause of the stop.
b) Reset the emergency stop button by pulling it outwards.
c) On the touchscreen, press "RESET" and then "ACKNOWLEDGE" for any alarms.
d) The press can then be restarted following the normal start-up sequence.
4.2.1 The firmware version is displayed on the touchscreen under "SETTINGS > ABOUT". The current firmware version is v4.2.1. This is the only version approved for use on Press Line 3. Do not install any other version without written authorisation from the Maintenance Manager.

4.2.2 The MPC SHALL be kept powered on at all times, except during maintenance work where the LOTO procedure (Section 2.1) is in force. The MPC does not have a separate power switch; it is powered from the control panel supply.

4.3 **Battery Replacement**

4.3.1 The MPC contains a lithium battery that maintains the real-time clock and stored parameters when the main supply is off. The battery is a CR2032 type.

4.3.2 The battery SHALL be replaced every 3 years or when a "BATTERY LOW" warning appears on the touchscreen.

4.3.3 Battery replacement procedure:

a) Isolate the control panel supply using the main isolator and apply LOTO.
b) Open the electrical cabinet door.
c) Locate the battery holder on the MPC main board (position marked "BATT1").
d) Note the current date and time settings before removing the battery, as these may be lost.
e) Remove the old battery and fit the new one, observing correct polarity.
f) Close the cabinet door and remove LOTO.
g) Restore power and check the touchscreen. If the date/time are incorrect, set them via "SETTINGS > DATE/TIME".

4.3.4 The old battery SHALL be disposed of in the designated battery recycling container in the maintenance workshop. Do not place it in general waste.

**5. TROUBLESHOOTING**

5.1 **General**

5.1.1 The following flowchart is a general guide to fault-finding on Press Line 3. Always start with the "Pre-Start Checklist" on the touchscreen, as many apparent faults are caused by simple setup issues.

5.1.2 If the press will not start, proceed as follows:

```
START
  |
  v
Is the main isolator ON? ----------- NO --> Turn it ON and retry
  |
 YES
  |
  v
Is the air supply pressure > 5 bar? -- NO --> Check main air valve and compressor
  |
 YES
  |
  v
Are any emergency stop buttons pressed? -- YES --> Reset them (Section 3.3)
  |
 NO
  |
  v
Are any guards open or interlocks tripped? -- YES --> Close guards and reset interlocks
  |
 NO
  |
  v
Is there an active alarm on the touchscreen? -- YES --> Read alarm text and follow advice
  |
 NO
  |
  v
Press START. Does the press rotate? -- NO --> Call maintenance (extension 215)
  |
 YES
  |
  v
Does the press reach set speed? -- NO --> Check ink supply and blanket pressure
  |
 YES
  |
  v
RUN NORMALLY
```

5.1.3 If the touchscreen is blank or frozen:

a) Wait 30 seconds. The MPC may be performing a background parameter save.
b) If still blank, press and hold the "POWER" symbol on the touchscreen for 5 seconds, then release. This forces a soft reset.
c) If the screen remains blank, isolate the control panel supply for 30 seconds, then restore power.
d) If the problem persists, contact the manufacturer's service desk. Do not open the MPC enclosure.

5.2 **Common Fault Codes**

| Fault Code | Description | Likely Cause | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-101 | Web break at infeed | Web tension too high, or splice failure | Re-thread web, reduce tension by 5% |
| E-102 | Web break at delivery | Blanket cylinder wrap | Clear wrap, check blanket pressure |
| E-110 | Registration error – side | Side lay misadjusted | Re-set side lay, check paper edge |
| E-112 | Registration error – circumferential | Draw rollers slipping | Check roller pressure, clean rollers |
| E-201 | Ink pump fault – unit 1 | Pump blocked or air lock | Clear pump, prime with ink |
| E-202 | Ink pump fault – unit 2 | Pump blocked or air lock | Clear pump, prime with ink |
| E-203 | Ink pump fault – unit 3 | Pump blocked or air lock | Clear pump, prime with ink |
| E-204 | Ink pump fault – unit 4 | Pump blocked or air lock | Clear pump, prime with ink |
| E-301 | Dampening solution level low | Tank empty or float stuck | Top up, check float |
| E-310 | Blanket wash cycle fault | Solenoid valve stuck | Check valve, clean or replace |
| E-401 | Drive fault – main motor | Overload or encoder fault | Check motor temperature, inspect encoder cable |

**2.4 Roles and Duties**

**2.4.1 Senior Maintenance Technician**

The Senior Maintenance Technician shall:

a) Be the first point of contact for all maintenance issues on Press Line 3, during both early and late shifts.
b) Carry out fault diagnosis on complex or recurring faults that have not been resolved by the shift technician.
c) Plan and allocate daily maintenance tasks, ensuring that the daily lubrication schedule (Section 6) is completed and signed off.

e) Check and sign the Maintenance Log Book (Form FM-PL3-01) at the start of each shift and at the end of each shift.
f) Ensure that all safety lockout procedures (Section 4) are followed before any maintenance work begins.
g) Order spare parts and consumables through the CMMS system, and verify that received parts match the order.
h) Liaise with the Shift Manager regarding press availability and any downtime that is likely to exceed 30 minutes.
i) Carry out the quarterly audit of the maintenance spares inventory.
j) Act as the appointed person for lifting operations, as defined in the Holbeck Print Works Lifting Policy.

**1.1 Purpose**

This manual defines the maintenance requirements, safety procedures, and repair standards for Press Line 3 at Holbeck Print Works. It is intended for use by maintenance technicians, press operators, and the Shift Manager. Compliance with the procedures in this manual is mandatory. The word “SHALL” indicates a mandatory action.

**1.2 Scope**

The manual covers the mechanical, electrical, and control systems of Press Line 3, including the reel stand, in-feed unit, printing units 1–4, dryer, chill rollers, folder unit, and the drive control panel (VFD-3). It does not cover the ancillary pre-press equipment or the binding line.

**1.3 Definitions and Abbreviations**

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| PLC | Programmable Logic Controller |
| VFD | Variable Frequency Drive |
| E-stop | Emergency Stop |
| LOTO | Lockout/Tagout |
| PM | Planned Maintenance |
| FM | Form (used with a number, e.g., FM-PL3-07) |

**1.4 Related Documents**

- Holbeck Print Works Lifting Policy (HPW-LP-01)
- Press Line 3 Operating Manual (OM-PL3)
- Health and Safety Policy (HPW-HS-02)

**2.1 Plant Engineer**

**2.2 Shift Manager**

**2.5 Press Operators**

Press operators shall report any unusual noise, vibration, or fault code immediately to the Shift Manager. Operators shall not attempt to repair any fault unless directed to do so by the Shift Manager or the Senior Maintenance Technician.

---

**3. PLANNED MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE**

**3.1 Daily Checks (Start of Shift)**

| Item | Check | Frequency | Action if Fault Found |
|------|-------|-----------|------------------------|
| 3.1.1 | Safety interlocks and E-stops | Each shift | Test all E-stops and interlocks. Do not run press until all pass. |
| 3.1.2 | Web tension sensors | Each shift | Verify sensor reading against known reference. |
| 3.1.3 | Air pressure | Each shift | Check main air supply is 6.5–7.0 bar. |
| 3.1.4 | Folder unit timing | Each shift | Confirm folder knife position against register marks. |

**3.2 Weekly Checks**

| Item | Check | Frequency | Action if Fault Found |
|------|-------|-----------|------------------------|
| 3.2.1 | Lubrication of gripper bar chain | Weekly | Grease per lubrication schedule (Section 3.4). |
| 3.2.2 | Bearing temperature (units 1–4) | Weekly | Use infrared thermometer. Replace bearing if > 80°C. |
| 3.2.3 | Sensor alignment (print units) | Weekly | Adjust per Section 5.3. |

**3.3 Monthly Checks**

| Item | Check | Frequency | Action if Fault Found |
|------|-------|-----------|------------------------|
| 3.3.1 | Gearbox oil level and condition | Monthly | Top up or replace per Section 3.5. |
| 3.3.2 | Compressed air filters | Monthly | Replace filter element if pressure drop > 0.2 bar. |
| 3.3.3 | Drive belt tension (reel stand) | Monthly | Adjust per Section 5.5. |

**3.4 Lubrication Schedule**

| Point | Lubricant | Interval | Method |
|-------|-----------|----------|--------|
| Gripper bar chain | ISO VG 150 gear oil | Weekly | Brush or drip feed; wipe excess. |
| Folder cam followers | Lithium grease EP2 | Monthly | Grease gun, 2 pumps per point. |
**3.5 Gearbox Oil Specification and Change Procedure**

| Gearbox | Oil Type | Capacity | Change Interval |
|---------|----------|----------|-----------------|
| Unit 1–4 main drive | ISO VG 220 mineral oil | 6.5 L each | 12 months or 4,000 hours, whichever comes first |
| Folder unit gearbox | ISO VG 320 mineral oil | 3.0 L | 12 months or 4,000 hours |
| Reel stand gearbox | ISO VG 150 mineral oil | 2.2 L | 6 months or 2,000 hours |

Oil change procedure:

1. Isolate the press at the main isolator and apply lockout per Section 2.2.
2. Place a suitable container beneath the drain plug. Drain oil while warm (operating temperature).
3. Remove and clean the magnetic drain plug. Inspect for metallic debris. If significant debris is found, record in the maintenance log and notify the Senior Maintenance Technician before refilling.
4. Refit the drain plug with a new washer. Torque to 40 N·m.
5. Fill with the specified oil through the fill point. Use a clean funnel or pump. Do not overfill.
6. Run the press at crawl speed for 5 minutes. Check for leaks and verify oil level. Top up if necessary.
7. Record the oil change in the maintenance log with date, hours run, and oil batch number.

**3.6 Compressed Air System**

The press air supply shall be maintained between 6.5 and 7.0 bar at the main regulator. The regulator is located on the wall adjacent to the reel stand. A pressure gauge is fitted on the press frame at each unit.

| Item | Check | Frequency | Action if Fault Found |
|------|-------|-----------|------------------------|
| Main regulator pressure | Each shift | See 3.1.3 | Adjust regulator; if unstable, report to Shift Manager. |
| Filter/regulator units (each unit) | Weekly | Drain condensate; check bowl for cracks. | Replace bowl if cracked or cloudy. |
| Air line fittings | Monthly | Check for leaks using soapy water. | Tighten or replace fitting. |
| Dryer desiccant | Monthly | Check colour indicator. | Replace desiccant if indicator shows saturation. |

---

**4. TROUBLESHOOTING**

The following table lists common faults, probable causes, and corrective actions. If a fault persists after the listed actions, or if the same fault recurs within one week, stop the press and contact the Senior Maintenance Technician.

| Fault | Probable Cause | Corrective Action |
|-------|----------------|-------------------|
| 4.1.1 Web break at splice | Incorrect splice tape; worn splice head | Re-splice per Section 6.2. Check splice head alignment. |
| 4.1.2 Web wander at infeed | Misaligned infeed rollers | Align rollers per Section 5.4. Check dancer roller bearings. |
| 4.1.3 Print registration drift | Sensor lens dirty; encoder coupling loose | Clean sensor lens with lint-free cloth. Check encoder coupling grub screws. |
| 4.1.4 Ink misting on units | Ink viscosity too low; dampening solution imbalance | Check viscosity per ink supplier spec. Adjust dampening per Section 7.2. |
| 4.1.5 Folder knife marks on product | Knife worn; timing out of adjustment | Inspect knife edge; replace if nicked. Adjust timing per Section 5.7. |
| 4.1.6 Gripper bar jam | Chain tension too low; gripper spring broken | Check chain tension. Replace gripper spring. |
| 4.1.7 Low air pressure alarm | Compressor fault; leaking hose | Check compressor pressure switch. Inspect hoses for leaks. |
| 4.1.8 Fault code E-214 (folder) | Folder cam sensor out of position | Re-position sensor per Section 5.8. |
| 4.1.9 Fault code E-107 (unit 2) | Blanket cylinder pressure too low | Re-set cylinder pressure per Section 5.9. |

**4.2 Troubleshooting Flowchart – Print Registration Drift**

Start: Register marks misaligned on product.

1. Is the sensor lens clean?
   - No → Clean lens. Re-test.
   - Yes → Go to 2.
2. Is the sensor mounting bracket tight?
   - No → Tighten bracket. Re-test.
   - Yes → Go to 3.
3. Is the encoder coupling secure?
   - No → Tighten or replace coupling. Re-test.
   - Yes → Go to 4.
4. Is the web tension stable?
   - No → Check dancer roller and air pressure. Re-test.
   - Yes → Go to 5.
5. Is the plate cylinder packing correct?
   - No → Re-pack per Section 5.10.
   - Yes → Contact Senior Maintenance Technician.

**3. Vehicle Logbooks**

Each vehicle in Fleet 7 has its own logbook. The logbook is the primary record for all servicing, inspections, and defects. It travels with the vehicle at all times.

3.1 Logbook contents, in order:
1. Vehicle identification page (registration, VIN, hub assignment)
2. PM service record (see Section 4)
3. Brake inspection record (see Section 6)
4. Tyre pressure and condition record (see Section 5)
5. Fuel consumption record (see Section 7)
6. Defect and repair log (open pages at the back)

3.2 Handover rules:
- The driver returning a vehicle at the end of a shift must complete the “End of Shift” box on the current page of the tyre pressure record, or write “NTR” (no tyre work required) if no check was due.

**6. Fuel Consumption Records**

6.1 Each vehicle in Fleet 7 has a fuel log card kept in the glovebox. The card is to be completed at
every fill-up, whether at the hub pump or at a commercial station. Entries must be made in
pencil so that corrections can be made legibly; do not use biro on the card as it smudges when
the card is handled in wet weather.

6.2 The following columns are printed on the card:

- Date (DD/MM/YYYY)
- Odometer reading at fill-up (miles)
- Litres pumped (to one decimal place)
- Cost (if purchased off-site)
- Driver initials

6.3 At the end of each week, the duty mechanic collects the fuel cards and transfers the figures
into the vehicle logbook. The logbook fuel summary table is laid out as follows:

| Vehicle | Week Ending | Odometer Start | Odometer End | Litres | Miles per Litre |
|---------|-------------|----------------|--------------|--------|-----------------|
| Van 7-01 | 15/06/2025 | 41,203 | 41,689 | 112.4 | 4.32 |
| Van 7-02 | 15/06/2025 | 38,915 | 39,402 | 118.1 | 4.12 |
| Van 7-03 | 15/06/2025 | 52,771 | 53,240 | 109.8 | 4.27 |

6.4 The miles-per-litre figure is calculated to two decimal places. Anything below 3.80 for a
Ford Transit Custom or below 3.60 for a Vauxhall Vivaro or Nissan NV250 should be flagged on
the logbook cover with a red diagonal line across the weekly entry, and the vehicle should be
booked in for a fuel system check before the next PM service.

6.5 Fuel cards are to be returned to the rack in the workshop office by 4:30 pm on Fridays.
Cards left in vehicles over the weekend will be treated as lost and a replacement issued. The
loss of three cards in a rolling twelve-month period results in a written note placed on the
driver's file.

6.6 Commercial station receipts must be stapled to the fuel card for the week. Do not use
paperclips, as they catch on the logbook rings. Receipts are kept for six months then shredded.

**7. Route Change Protocols**

7.1 Temporary route changes are authorised by the Distribution Coordinator only. A temporary
change is defined as any alteration to the published route that lasts for more than one working
day but less than six weeks. Changes expected to last six weeks or longer must be treated as
permanent and submitted through the formal route revision process (Section 7.4).

7.2 When a temporary route change is approved, the coordinator issues a yellow Route Change
Notice (RCN) form. The form must be kept in the vehicle's document wallet, on top of the
route sheet, for the duration of the change. The following information is recorded on the RCN:

- RCN number (sequential, starting RCN-2025-001 each calendar year)
- Date issued
- Route number affected
- Reason for the change
- New stopping order or road closures, as applicable
- Expected duration
- Coordinator's signature

7.3 At the end of the temporary change period, the driver returns the RCN to the workshop
office. The returned form is filed in the route change folder. If a change is extended beyond
the original expected duration, the coordinator must issue a new RCN with a new number; the
original RCN is marked "SUPERSEDED" in red and filed. Do not amend the original RCN.

7.4 Permanent route revisions are handled as follows:

a) The Distribution Coordinator prepares a draft route sheet showing the proposed stopping
order, timings, and any changed mileage.

b) The draft is circulated to all drivers who work that route. Drivers have five working days
to submit comments or objections in writing. Verbal objections are not recorded.

c) The coordinator reviews the comments and either adopts the draft, amends it, or withdraws
it. If amended, the revised draft is circulated again for a further three working days.

d) Once adopted, the route sheet is printed on white paper, stamped "APPROVED", and dated.
The previous route sheet is stamped "OBSOLETE – KEEP FOR REFERENCE" and moved to the
obsolete routes folder in the filing cabinet.

e) The approved route sheet is laminated and placed in the vehicle document wallet. A copy is
also pinned to the noticeboard in the drivers' room.

---

**1. INTRODUCTION**

1.1 This manual provides standard procedures, specifications, and safety information for the operation and maintenance of Press Line 3. It is intended for use by trained maintenance technicians, press operators, and shift supervisors.

1.2 All maintenance activities SHALL be carried out in accordance with the procedures in this manual. Any deviation from these procedures requires prior written authorisation from the Maintenance Manager.

1.3 The manual is divided into numbered sections. Section numbers are referenced throughout. Where a section has been revised, the revision stamp and date are shown in the footer of each page.

1.4 Any defects, missing parts, or suspected safety issues SHALL be reported immediately using the Exception Log (Form MP-EL-01) and the relevant section of this manual flagged for review.

---

**2. GENERAL SAFETY**

2.1 **Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) Procedure**

2.1.1 Before any maintenance, cleaning, or repair work is carried out, the following lockout procedure SHALL be followed:

a) Isolate the main electrical supply using the isolator switch located at the rear of the press, adjacent to the control cabinet. The switch is labelled "PL3 MAIN ISOLATOR". (Note: As of revision 1.4, this switch is a new red rotary type; the old toggle switch has been removed.)
b) Lock the isolator in the OFF position using a personal padlock. Each technician SHALL use their own lock and key.
c) Depress and lock the pneumatic isolation valve on the air supply line (red valve, located near the floor on the left-hand side of the press).
d) If work is to be carried out on the blanket cylinders or the impression cylinder, also isolate the hydraulic supply and lock the pressure release valve.
e) Verify that all moving parts have come to a complete stop before proceeding.
f) Place a "DANGER - DO NOT OPERATE" tag on the main isolator and on the control panel.

2.1.2 Only the person who fitted a lock may remove it. If a lock is left on and the person has gone off shift, the shift supervisor SHALL verify the situation and may remove the lock only after ensuring it is safe to do so, and the removal SHALL be logged in the Exception Log.

The Maintenance Manual - Press Line 3 states that the scheduled_overhaul_date for Press Line 3 is 2023-08-14. Record status: superseded.

2.1.3 On completion of work, remove all tools and materials, check that no personnel are in the danger zone, and then remove locks and tags in the reverse order of fitting.

2.2 **Emergency Stop**

2.2.1 There are three red emergency stop buttons on Press Line 3: one at the feeder end, one at the delivery end, and one on the main control panel. Pressing any one of these SHALL immediately cut power to all drives and stop the press.

2.2.2 After an emergency stop, the cause SHALL be investigated before restarting. The restart procedure is described in Section 3.4.

---

**3. OPERATING PROCEDURES**

3.1 **Start-Up Sequence (Normal)**

a) Ensure all guards are in place and secure.
b) Check that the LOTO tags are clear (if any work has been carried out).
c) Turn on the main isolator.
d) Turn on the air supply at the main valve.
e) Switch on the control panel power.
f) Wait for the touchscreen to initialise (approx. 30 seconds).
g) Perform the "Pre-Start Checklist" displayed on the touchscreen. This includes checking ink levels, blanket pressure, and web alignment.
h) Press "START" on the touchscreen. The press will slowly rotate and then speed up to the set speed.

3.2 **Shut-Down Sequence**

a) Stop the web feed using the "WEB STOP" button.
b) Run the press at low speed for 2 minutes to clear the last of the web.
c) Apply the blanket wash cycle (see Section 6.2).
d) Press "STOP" on the touchscreen.
e) Switch off the control panel power.
f) Turn off the air supply.
g) Turn off the main isolator.

3.3 **Emergency Restart After E-Stop**

3.3.1 If an emergency stop has been activated, the following steps SHALL be taken:

a) Investigate and rectify the cause of the stop.
b) Reset the emergency stop button by pulling it outwards.
c) On the touchscreen, press "RESET" and then "ACKNOWLEDGE" for any alarms.
d) The press can then be restarted following the normal start-up sequence.

4.2.2 The MPC SHALL be kept powered on at all times, except during maintenance work where the LOTO procedure (Section 2.1) is in force. The MPC does not have a separate power switch; it is powered from the control panel supply.

4.3 **Battery Replacement**

4.3.1 The MPC contains a lithium battery that maintains the real-time clock and stored parameters when the main supply is off. The battery is a CR2032 type.

4.3.2 The battery SHALL be replaced every 3 years or when a "BATTERY LOW" warning appears on the touchscreen.

4.3.3 Battery replacement procedure:

a) Isolate the control panel supply using the main isolator and apply LOTO.
b) Open the electrical cabinet door.
c) Locate the battery holder on the MPC main board (position marked "BATT1").
d) Note the current date and time settings before removing the battery, as these may be lost.
e) Remove the old battery and fit the new one, observing correct polarity.
f) Close the cabinet door and remove LOTO.
g) Restore power and check the touchscreen. If the date/time are incorrect, set them via "SETTINGS > DATE/TIME".

4.3.4 The old battery SHALL be disposed of in the designated battery recycling container in the maintenance workshop. Do not place it in general waste.

5.1.1 The following flowchart is a general guide to fault-finding on Press Line 3. Always start with the "Pre-Start Checklist" on the touchscreen, as many apparent faults are caused by simple setup issues.

5.1.2 If the press will not start, proceed as follows:

Is the main isolator ON? ----------- NO --> Turn it ON and retry
  |

Is the air supply pressure > 5 bar? -- NO --> Check main air valve and compressor
  |

Are any emergency stop buttons pressed? -- YES --> Reset them (Section 3.3)

documents.title: Maintenance Manual - Press Line 3
documents.content:
**1.1 Purpose**

This manual defines the maintenance requirements, safety procedures, and repair standards for Press Line 3 at Holbeck Print Works. It is intended for use by maintenance technicians, press operators, and the Shift Manager. Compliance with the procedures in this manual is mandatory. The word “SHALL” indicates a mandatory action.

**1.2 Scope**

The manual covers the mechanical, electrical, and control systems of Press Line 3, including the reel stand, in-feed unit, printing units 1–4, dryer, chill rollers, folder unit, and the drive control panel (VFD-3). It does not cover the ancillary pre-press equipment or the binding line.

**1.3 Definitions and Abbreviations**

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| PLC | Programmable Logic Controller |
| VFD | Variable Frequency Drive |
| E-stop | Emergency Stop |
| LOTO | Lockout/Tagout |
| PM | Planned Maintenance |
| FM | Form (used with a number, e.g., FM-PL3-07) |

**1.4 Related Documents**

- Holbeck Print Works Lifting Policy (HPW-LP-01)
- Press Line 3 Operating Manual (OM-PL3)
- Health and Safety Policy (HPW-HS-02)
- Spare Parts Catalogue – Press Line 3 (SP-PL3)

---

**2. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**2.1 Plant Engineer**

The Plant Engineer owns this manual and shall approve all revisions. The Plant Engineer shall also approve any change to the appointment of the Senior Maintenance Technician.

**2.2 Shift Manager**

The Shift Manager shall ensure that maintenance activities do not compromise press safety or production schedules. The Shift Manager shall be notified of any downtime likely to exceed 30 minutes.

**2.3 Senior Maintenance Technician**

The Maintenance Manual - Press Line 3 has revision_number Rev 7. Record status: current. The current revision of this manual is Rev 7, authorised on 2025-11-01, and this is the revision in force until a formal change of appointment is issued in writing. Any proposed change to this appointment shall be made by the Plant Engineer and notified to the Shift Manager and the Health and Safety Representative.

**2.4 Maintenance Technicians**

**2.5 Press Operators**

Press operators shall report any unusual noise, vibration, or fault code immediately to the Shift Manager. Operators shall not attempt to repair any fault unless directed to do so by the Shift Manager or the Senior Maintenance Technician.

---

**3. PLANNED MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE**

**3.1 Daily Checks (Start of Shift)**

| Item | Check | Frequency | Action if Fault Found |
|------|-------|-----------|------------------------|
| 3.1.1 | Safety interlocks and E-stops | Each shift | Test all E-stops and interlocks. Do not run press until all pass. |
| 3.1.2 | Web tension sensors | Each shift | Verify sensor reading against known reference. |
| 3.1.3 | Air pressure | Each shift | Check main air supply is 6.5–7.0 bar. |
| 3.1.4 | Folder unit timing | Each shift | Confirm folder knife position against register marks. |

**3.2 Weekly Checks**

| Item | Check | Frequency | Action if Fault Found |
|------|-------|-----------|------------------------|
| 3.2.1 | Lubrication of gripper bar chain | Weekly | Grease per lubrication schedule (Section 3.4). |
| 3.2.2 | Bearing temperature (units 1–4) | Weekly | Use infrared thermometer. Replace bearing if > 80°C. |
| 3.2.3 | Sensor alignment (print units) | Weekly | Adjust per Section 5.3. |

**3.3 Monthly Checks**

| Item | Check | Frequency | Action if Fault Found |
|------|-------|-----------|------------------------|
| 3.3.1 | Gearbox oil level and condition | Monthly | Top up or replace per Section 3.5. |
| 3.3.2 | Compressed air filters | Monthly | Replace filter element if pressure drop > 0.2 bar. |
| 3.3.3 | Drive belt tension (reel stand) | Monthly | Adjust per Section 5.5. |

**3.4 Lubrication Schedule**

| Point | Lubricant | Interval | Method |
|-------|-----------|----------|--------|
| Gripper bar chain | ISO VG 150 gear oil | Weekly | Brush or drip feed; wipe excess. |
| Folder cam followers | Lithium grease EP2 | Monthly | Grease gun, 2 pumps per point. |

documents.title: Maintenance Manual - Press Line 3
documents.content:
**3.5 Gearbox Oil Specification and Change Procedure**

| Gearbox | Oil Type | Capacity | Change Interval |
|---------|----------|----------|-----------------|
| Unit 1–4 main drive | ISO VG 220 mineral oil | 6.5 L each | 12 months or 4,000 hours, whichever comes first |
| Folder unit gearbox | ISO VG 320 mineral oil | 3.0 L | 12 months or 4,000 hours |
| Reel stand gearbox | ISO VG 150 mineral oil | 2.2 L | 6 months or 2,000 hours |

Oil change procedure:

1. Isolate the press at the main isolator and apply lockout per Section 2.2.
2. Place a suitable container beneath the drain plug. Drain oil while warm (operating temperature).
3. Remove and clean the magnetic drain plug. Inspect for metallic debris. If significant debris is found, record in the maintenance log and notify the Senior Maintenance Technician before refilling.
4. Refit the drain plug with a new washer. Torque to 40 N·m.
5. Fill with the specified oil through the fill point. Use a clean funnel or pump. Do not overfill.
6. Run the press at crawl speed for 5 minutes. Check for leaks and verify oil level. Top up if necessary.
7. Record the oil change in the maintenance log with date, hours run, and oil batch number.

**3.6 Compressed Air System**

The press air supply shall be maintained between 6.5 and 7.0 bar at the main regulator. The regulator is located on the wall adjacent to the reel stand. A pressure gauge is fitted on the press frame at each unit.

| Item | Check | Frequency | Action if Fault Found |
|------|-------|-----------|------------------------|
| Main regulator pressure | Each shift | See 3.1.3 | Adjust regulator; if unstable, report to Shift Manager. |
| Filter/regulator units (each unit) | Weekly | Drain condensate; check bowl for cracks. | Replace bowl if cracked or cloudy. |
| Air line fittings | Monthly | Check for leaks using soapy water. | Tighten or replace fitting. |
| Dryer desiccant | Monthly | Check colour indicator. | Replace desiccant if indicator shows saturation. |

---

**4. TROUBLESHOOTING**

The following table lists common faults, probable causes, and corrective actions. If a fault persists after the listed actions, or if the same fault recurs within one week, stop the press and contact the Senior Maintenance Technician.

| Fault | Probable Cause | Corrective Action |
|-------|----------------|-------------------|
| 4.1.1 Web break at splice | Incorrect splice tape; worn splice head | Re-splice per Section 6.2. Check splice head alignment. |
| 4.1.2 Web wander at infeed | Misaligned infeed rollers | Align rollers per Section 5.4. Check dancer roller bearings. |
| 4.1.3 Print registration drift | Sensor lens dirty; encoder coupling loose | Clean sensor lens with lint-free cloth. Check encoder coupling grub screws. |
| 4.1.4 Ink misting on units | Ink viscosity too low; dampening solution imbalance | Check viscosity per ink supplier spec. Adjust dampening per Section 7.2. |
| 4.1.5 Folder knife marks on product | Knife worn; timing out of adjustment | Inspect knife edge; replace if nicked. Adjust timing per Section 5.7. |
| 4.1.6 Gripper bar jam | Chain tension too low; gripper spring broken | Check chain tension. Replace gripper spring. |
| 4.1.7 Low air pressure alarm | Compressor fault; leaking hose | Check compressor pressure switch. Inspect hoses for leaks. |
| 4.1.8 Fault code E-214 (folder) | Folder cam sensor out of position | Re-position sensor per Section 5.8. |
| 4.1.9 Fault code E-107 (unit 2) | Blanket cylinder pressure too low | Re-set cylinder pressure per Section 5.9. |

**4.2 Troubleshooting Flowchart – Print Registration Drift**

Start: Register marks misaligned on product.

1. Is the sensor lens clean?
   - No → Clean lens. Re-test.
   - Yes → Go to 2.
2. Is the sensor mounting bracket tight?
   - No → Tighten bracket. Re-test.
   - Yes → Go to 3.
3. Is the encoder coupling secure?
   - No → Tighten or replace coupling. Re-test.
   - Yes → Go to 4.
4. Is the web tension stable?
   - No → Check dancer roller and air pressure. Re-test.
   - Yes → Go to 5.
5. Is the plate cylinder packing correct?
   - No → Re-pack per Section 5.10.
   - Yes → Contact Senior Maintenance Technician.

This is a controlled document. Any printed copy is uncontrolled when separated from the master file in the Fleet Services office. The current revision number is **Rev 4**. Superseded revisions are retained in the archive folder labelled “DVF7 Manual – prior issues” in the top drawer of the filing cabinet next to the kettle. Do not discard old issues; they are kept for audit.

---

**3. Vehicle Logbooks**

Each vehicle in Fleet 7 has its own logbook. The logbook is the primary record for all servicing, inspections, and defects. It travels with the vehicle at all times.

3.1 Logbook contents, in order:
1. Vehicle identification page (registration, VIN, hub assignment)
2. PM service record (see Section 4)
3. Brake inspection record (see Section 6)
4. Tyre pressure and condition record (see Section 5)
5. Fuel consumption record (see Section 7)
6. Defect and repair log (open pages at the back)

3.2 Handover rules:
- The driver returning a vehicle at the end of a shift must complete the “End of Shift” box on the current page of the tyre pressure record, or write “NTR” (no tyre work required) if no check was due.
- The driver taking over a vehicle must check the logbook for any open defect entries before leaving the yard.
- If a logbook is missing or damaged, the vehicle is not to be used. Report to the fleet coordinator immediately. Do not substitute scraps of paper.

---

The Maintenance Manual - Delivery Van Fleet 7 has revision_number Rev 4. Record status: current.

**4. Preventive Maintenance (PM) Service Intervals**

PM services are scheduled by miles or calendar months, whichever comes first. All intervals are counted from the previous service completion date or odometer reading.

| Service Code | Interval | Work Summary |
|--------------|----------|--------------|
| PM-A | 6,000 miles or 6 months | Oil and filter change, fluid top-ups, visual inspection of belts and hoses, tyre pressures and tread check, brake pad measurement (front and rear), road test. |
| PM-B | 12,000 miles or 12 months | All PM-A items plus: fuel filter replacement, air filter check (replace if visibly dirty), battery load test, brake fluid sample, suspension and steering inspection, wheel bearing check, exhaust system check, full underbody inspection. |
| PM-C | 24,000 miles or 24 months | All PM-B items plus: coolant replacement, gearbox oil check, drive belt replacement (if fitted), clutch adjustment check, brake fluid replacement, wheel alignment check, DPF inspection (Ford and Nissan only). |

3.1 (sic – see Section 4.1 below) PM service records are kept in the logbook. Each entry must include:
- Date (DD/MM/YYYY)
- Odometer reading at service
- Service code (PM-A, PM-B, or PM-C)
- Name and initials of the mechanic performing the work
- Any parts replaced (part number if available)
- Any additional work recommended

4.1 Correction to numbering: The above table is the full PM schedule. There is no separate Section 3.1 in this manual; the logbook rules in Section 3 apply. The stray “3.1” above was a typo in the Rev 4 drafting and has been left in place for continuity with the printed copies issued on 2025-06-15. It does not affect the schedule.

---

documents.content:
**6. Fuel Consumption Records**

6.1 Each vehicle in Fleet 7 has a fuel log card kept in the glovebox. The card is to be completed at
every fill-up, whether at the hub pump or at a commercial station. Entries must be made in
pencil so that corrections can be made legibly; do not use biro on the card as it smudges when
the card is handled in wet weather.

6.2 The following columns are printed on the card:

- Date (DD/MM/YYYY)
- Odometer reading at fill-up (miles)
- Litres pumped (to one decimal place)
- Cost (if purchased off-site)
- Driver initials

6.3 At the end of each week, the duty mechanic collects the fuel cards and transfers the figures
into the vehicle logbook. The logbook fuel summary table is laid out as follows:

| Vehicle | Week Ending | Odometer Start | Odometer End | Litres | Miles per Litre |
|---------|-------------|----------------|--------------|--------|-----------------|
| Van 7-01 | 15/06/2025 | 41,203 | 41,689 | 112.4 | 4.32 |
| Van 7-02 | 15/06/2025 | 38,915 | 39,402 | 118.1 | 4.12 |
| Van 7-03 | 15/06/2025 | 52,771 | 53,240 | 109.8 | 4.27 |

6.4 The miles-per-litre figure is calculated to two decimal places. Anything below 3.80 for a
Ford Transit Custom or below 3.60 for a Vauxhall Vivaro or Nissan NV250 should be flagged on
the logbook cover with a red diagonal line across the weekly entry, and the vehicle should be
booked in for a fuel system check before the next PM service.

6.5 Fuel cards are to be returned to the rack in the workshop office by 4:30 pm on Fridays.
Cards left in vehicles over the weekend will be treated as lost and a replacement issued. The
loss of three cards in a rolling twelve-month period results in a written note placed on the
driver's file.

6.6 Commercial station receipts must be stapled to the fuel card for the week. Do not use
paperclips, as they catch on the logbook rings. Receipts are kept for six months then shredded.

**7. Route Change Protocols**

7.1 Temporary route changes are authorised by the Distribution Coordinator only. A temporary
change is defined as any alteration to the published route that lasts for more than one working
day but less than six weeks. Changes expected to last six weeks or longer must be treated as
permanent and submitted through the formal route revision process (Section 7.4).

7.2 When a temporary route change is approved, the coordinator issues a yellow Route Change
Notice (RCN) form. The form must be kept in the vehicle's document wallet, on top of the
route sheet, for the duration of the change. The following information is recorded on the RCN:

- RCN number (sequential, starting RCN-2025-001 each calendar year)
- Date issued
- Route number affected
- Reason for the change
- New stopping order or road closures, as applicable
- Expected duration
- Coordinator's signature

7.3 At the end of the temporary change period, the driver returns the RCN to the workshop
office. The returned form is filed in the route change folder. If a change is extended beyond
the original expected duration, the coordinator must issue a new RCN with a new number; the
original RCN is marked "SUPERSEDED" in red and filed. Do not amend the original RCN.

7.4 Permanent route revisions are handled as follows:

a) The Distribution Coordinator prepares a draft route sheet showing the proposed stopping
order, timings, and any changed mileage.

b) The draft is circulated to all drivers who work that route. Drivers have five working days
to submit comments or objections in writing. Verbal objections are not recorded.

c) The coordinator reviews the comments and either adopts the draft, amends it, or withdraws
it. If amended, the revised draft is circulated again for a further three working days.

d) Once adopted, the route sheet is printed on white paper, stamped "APPROVED", and dated.
The previous route sheet is stamped "OBSOLETE – KEEP FOR REFERENCE" and moved to the
obsolete routes folder in the filing cabinet.

e) The approved route sheet is laminated and placed in the vehicle document wallet. A copy is
also pinned to the noticeboard in the drivers' room.
